name: Interest Explorer
description: How much would you enjoy each activity? There are no right or wrong answers.
framework: Holland RIASEC interest theory (public). All items are original to PRISM.

items.prompt: Repairing a bicycle or a ceiling fan that has stopped working
Building a working model, like a solar car, for a science fair
Working outdoors on a farm, a construction site or in a workshop
Using tools or machines such as a drill, a soldering iron or a 3D printer
Finding out why a plant grows faster under one kind of light than another
Spending an hour on a tricky maths or logic puzzle
Reading about how vaccines or rockets actually work
Running an experiment and analysing the results in a table or graph
Designing a poster, logo or comic strip
Writing a story, poem or script
Composing music, dancing or acting in a play
Photographing or filming something in an original way
Teaching a younger student a topic they find difficult
Volunteering at a health camp or community event
Listening to a friend's problem and helping them think it through
Organising activities for children or elderly people
Starting a small business, such as selling snacks or crafts at a school fair
Persuading a group to support your idea
Leading a team for a competition or school event
Negotiating a better price or deal
Keeping accounts for a club or a family shop
Organising files, data or a timetable so everything is easy to find
Checking a report carefully for errors
Following a clear step-by-step procedure to finish a task accurately
